outputDir.why: THE ACT BINDING, and the one fact that says WHICH act this per-GAME document governs. The consumer reads one input file and writes zone_bg.bin / bg_tiles.bin / bg_anim.emp / bg_anim_banks.bin into ONE hardcoded directory, so the document describes exactly the act whose generated data lives there — not every act in the project. Nothing inside the document names an act; this literal is the whole of the binding, which is why it is vendored here rather than inferred. Aurora matches it against project.json's per-act `stripPath` (the same project-root-relative directory) and treats a project whose acts point elsewhere as having NO overridden act — the safe direction, since the document then governs nothing Aurora is showing. SEAM, reported to aeon: the pairing is a coincidence of two hardcodes, one per repo. Closing it means aeon deriving OUT_DIR from project.json (or naming the act in the document) rather than both sides spelling the same path.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `OUT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'games', 'sonic4', 'data', 'generated', 'ojz', 'act1')`, and every write in `main()` is `os.path.join(OUT_DIR, ...)`: zone_bg.bin, bg_tiles.bin, bg_anim.emp, bg_anim_banks.bin, ojz_palette.bin

BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT.why: Not enforced by this codec — recorded because it is what makes the PREFIX identity an identity: a band's DMA destination is BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM + slot_base*32 with BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM = $8000, and 1024 * 32 = $8000 IS the tile blob's own base. So slot 0 is literally tiles[0]; bands DMA OVER the static blob's leading slots, never beside them.
authorities: aeon tools/vram_map.py:25 — `BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT = 1024`
aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM = 0x8000`; `vram_dest = BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM + b['slot_base'] * 32`; and the layout rebase `(idx + BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT) & 0x7FF`

TILE_BYTES.why: One 8x8 4bpp tile. `col_bytes = rows * TILE_BYTES` is the quantity required to be a power of two.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `col_bytes = rows * 32`
aeon engine/level/bg_anim.emp — `const TILE_BYTES_SHIFT = 5  // log2(32 bytes per 8x8 tile)`

TILE_PIXELS.why: Each tile in `tiles` and in every `phases` bank is a flat array of exactly this many pixel values, row-major 8x8.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — the pack loop `for row in range(8): for col in range(4)` indexes `t[row*8 + col*2]` and `t[row*8 + col*2 + 1]`, whose highest index is 63

TILE_PIXEL_MAX.why: 4bpp. The consumer MASKS rather than rejects (`hi = t[...] & 0xF`), so a 16 bakes silently as a 0 — which is why the writer refuses out-of-range instead of relying on the mask.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `hi = t[row*8 + col*2] & 0xF`
empyrean docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md §5 — writer-normative: `each tile = cols*rows tiles, each tile = 64 pixel values 0..15`

TILE_WIDTH_PX.why: `pattern_px` must equal `cols * TILE_WIDTH_PX` — the pattern's width in pixels, from which the consumer derives `step_mask = pattern_px - 1`.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `assert pattern_px == cols * 8, 'pattern width must equal cols*8'`

BG_LAYOUT_WORDS.why: 64x64 nametable words, the post-pad length the consumer asserts.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `assert len(layout) == 4096, 'layout must be 64x32 or 64x64 words'`; `COLS, ROWS = 64, 64`

BG_LAYOUT_WORDS_LEGACY.why: 64x32. The consumer ZERO-PADS it to 4096 rather than refusing, so a legacy file is legal input. This codec accepts it and does NOT rewrite it: silently re-lengthening someone's layout is an unrequested edit, and the pad is the consumer's business.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `if len(layout) == 2048: layout = layout + [0]*2048  # legacy 32-row layout: pad to 64 rows`

LAYOUT_WORD_MAX.why: Each layout entry is packed big-endian unsigned 16-bit; anything outside 0..65535 raises inside the consumer rather than baking.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `struct.pack_into('>H', nt, (col * ROWS + row) * 2, word)`

LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK.why: The low bits of a layout word hold the BLOB-LOCAL tile index; every bit above them is the Genesis nametable's own attribute field (priority / palette line / flips), which the consumer PRESERVES verbatim. A writer that renumbers `tiles` must therefore rewrite `word & LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK` and leave `word & ~LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK` alone. THE ESCAPE MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE MASK: the consumer rebases only `if word != 0`, so a layout word of EXACTLY zero is passed through unrebased and renders VRAM tile 0 (blank) — it does NOT mean tiles[0]. A renumbering that turns a nonzero word into zero, or a zero word into nonzero, silently changes what that cell renders while every other assert in the consumer still passes.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — the nametable loop: `if word != 0: idx = word & 0x7FF; word = (word & ~0x7FF) | ((idx + BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT) & 0x7FF)`

A driver names the SCALAR SOURCE only: every band moves HORIZONTALLY whichever driver it picks (bg_anim.emp: 'Each band is a horizontally-periodic pattern'). `camera_y` does NOT mean vertical motion.

topLevelKeys.$comment: Declaration order IS the canonical write order (aeon EFFECTS_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md §1.1 table order). `ownership` is Aurora's, per the 2026-08-22 sole-writer ruling (aurora docs/reviews/2026-08-22-bg-override-ownership-ruling.md §5; empyrean AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md §5.2).

anims.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `anims = data.get('anims')`; absent or falsy -> the disabled stub (band_count = 0)
anims.emptyIsUnauthored: aeon tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCoherence::test_live_override_file_is_coherent_if_it_has_bands asserts `assertNotIn('anims', live)` when there are no bands, with the reason 'an empty `anims` key is neither absent nor authored'. That binds the WRITER: Aurora never emits an empty array. It does NOT bind the reader — inject_editor_bg.py bakes such a document as the disabled stub without complaint, so refusing to open it would make Aurora unable to load a file its own consumer accepts. The reader therefore DROPS the key and reports it in notices; the refusal lives on the write path, which is the boundary that can enforce it. The single exception is an empty `anims` beside a legacy `anim`: the consumer's fallback is keyed on `anims is None`, so an empty array suppresses it and the band is silently dropped — there the emptiness is load-bearing and normalizing would be a guess, so the reader refuses.

anim.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `if anims is None and data.get('anim'): anims = [data['anim']]`
anim.writerRule: aeon EFFECTS_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md §1.1: 'LEGACY single-band form … Writers must not emit it (read-side compatibility only)'. This codec therefore UPGRADES it on read (anim -> anims[0]) and refuses to serialize a document still carrying it — the only behaviour that neither emits the legacy key nor destroys the band it holds.

invariants.columnBytesPowerOfTwo: rows * TILE_BYTES must be a power of two (the consumer derives col_shift = log2 of it and asserts the round trip)
invariants.contiguousPacking: bands pack contiguously from slot 0 in list order; slot_base, when present, must equal the running cursor
invariants.insideTheBlob: slot_base + cols*rows <= len(tiles) for every band
invariants.prefixIdentity: phases[0] == tiles[slot_base : slot_base + cols*rows] — the band's rest state IS the static tiles it covers. This is the invariant that makes anims/tiles/layout ONE unit rather than three separable keys: a violation bakes CLEANLY and ships silently corrupt art, and every other assert in the consumer still passes (aeon docs/BUGS.md TOOL-01; tools/bg_override_io.py's docstring; aeon tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCoherence).
invariants.capacity: len(tiles) <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY. Animated slots are a PREFIX of tiles, NOT an addition — they cost no capacity beyond the array that already holds them (empyrean §5.1, which corrects an earlier `tiles + animated slots <= 448` rule that would have told Aurora the flagship act cannot carry any band at all).
invariants.layoutTileIndex: layout[row*64 + col] is a nametable word whose low LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK bits are a blob-local index into `tiles` and whose remaining bits are attributes the consumer preserves — EXCEPT that a word of exactly 0 is passed through unrebased and renders VRAM tile 0 (blank) rather than tiles[0]. Adding or removing a band renumbers `tiles`, so every nonzero word must be rewritten INDEX-ONLY, and a rewrite that would produce the value 0 is unrepresentable rather than merely different.
